questions.title: The garden wall round the gate court

evidence.title: 日下舊聞考 大宫门
evidence.excerpt_zh: 大宫門五楹門前左右朝房各五楹其後東為宗人府内閣吏部禮部兵部都察院理藩院翰林院詹事府國子監鑾儀衛東四旗各衙門直房東夾道内為銀庫又東北為南書房東南為檔案房西為户部刑部工部欽天監内務府光禄寺通政司大理寺鴻臚寺太常寺太僕寺御書處上駟院武備院西四旗各衙門直房西夾道之西南為造辦處又南為藥房
evidence.summary: The main gate has five bays with five-bay court offices left and right. Behind them the duty rooms of the boards and offices are set out east and west by name, with the silver vault, 南書房 Southern Study and archive room to the east and the 造辦處 Imperial Workshops and pharmacy to the south-west.

evidence.title: The Great Palace Gate and the offices before it
evidence.excerpt_other: The Great Palace Gate was a roofed building in which hung a tablet inscribed with the name of the garden, Yuan Ming Yuan, written by the Emperor K'ang Hsi.
evidence.summary: 大宫门 Da Gongmen: waiting rooms beside the road, behind them offices of the boards and the Eight Banners, the Grand Council, the 南书房 imperial school, treasury, dispensary and kitchens. Note 15 on p.70 lists the offices east and west of the gate by name.

evidence.title: 圆明园银库：清朝兴衰晴雨表
evidence.summary: Traces the 圆明园 treasury as one of three in the Imperial Household's finances: its growth as a measure of Qing strength and of the garden's rise, and its decline to the plunder of 1860 by British and French troops.

searched: No picture of it found in the Forty Scenes album, its 1745 woodcuts, the Bertin gouaches and the 1887 lithograph; the 20 Xiyang Lou plates; ruin photographs on Commons, at Östasiatiska museet, the Slovene Ethnographic Museum, Historical Photographs of China, the Rijksmuseum, Wellcome and in NDL's albums of about 1900; today's photographs on Commons.

plan_ref.text: Drawn on the plan of the gardens (S01), labelled 银库.
